newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas shares end flat as market awaits wage news.
newsitem.headline: Caracas shares end flat as market awaits wage news.

text.p: Share prices on the Caracas Stock Exchange closed fractionally lower in moderate trade as the market awaited news on the upcoming announcement of a new minimum salary, brokers said. According to preliminary figures from the exchange, the market's 19-share .IBC index slipped 0.08 percent to 6,236.07.

A minimum salary raise of 44 percent to 75,000 bolivars ($156) per month 44 percent, was announced after the close. The increase was roughly in line with market expectations and was unlikely to affect prices once trading resumed Friday following the May 1 Labor Day holiday, brokers said.
A total of 21 stocks fell, 11 rose and 10 closed flat in trade of 2.9 billion bolivars ($6.1 million).

"People are waiting to see what the president is going to announce about the salary bonus," said Valores Occidental broker Miguel Ramirez, who added that the market was also waiting for news on planned electricity rates and gasoline prices.
The composite .MRCP Merinvest index, which includes telephone company CANTV, however rose 0.40 percent to 96.58.
CANTV reported a per share profit of $0.13 in the first quarter of 1997 earlier Wednesday, up from a $0.13 loss in the same period last year.
CANTV stock rose 46.00 bolivars to 2,057.00 bolivars and Electricidad de Caracas edged up 2.00 bolivars to 522.00 bolivars.
